title: Fix the sharded GEMM
starter:
%A    = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=0
%B    = buffer 16 dtype=f32 slot=1
%C    = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=2
%acc  = alloc 4 dtype=f32
%d    = range 2 axis=device
%b    = range 4 axis=global
%t    = range 4 axis=local
%k    = range 4
%da   = mul %d 4
%ds   = mul %d 16
%br   = mul %b 4
%ao0  = add %da %br
%ao   = add %ao0 %k
%av   = shrink %A %ao []
%a    = load %av
%bo0  = mul %k 4
%bo   = add %bo0 %t
%bv   = shrink %B %bo []
%bb   = load %bv
%cv   = shrink %acc %t []
%cur  = load %cv
%p    = mul %a %bb
%sum  = add %cur %p
%st   = store %cv %sum
%ek   = end %st %k
%et   = end %ek %t
%acc1 = after %acc %et
%u    = range 4 axis=local
%rv   = shrink %acc1 %u []
%res  = load %rv
%co0  = add %ds %br
%co   = add %co0 %u
%ov   = shrink %C %co []
%sc   = store %ov %res
%eu   = end %sc %u
%eb   = end %et %eu %b
%ed   = end %eb %d
%C1   = after %C %ed
hints: C's rows 0 to 3 come out right and rows 4 to 7 do not, so look at how device 1 finds its rows of A. Compare A's offset with C's.
Device 1 starts at row 4. A row of A is 4 elements long, so row 4 starts at element 16, not element 4.
Use %ds for A as well: %ao0 = add %ds %br. Then delete the %da line, which nothing uses any more.

answer.code:
%A    = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=0
%B    = buffer 16 dtype=f32 slot=1
%C    = buffer 32 dtype=f32 slot=2
%acc  = alloc 4 dtype=f32
%d    = range 2 axis=device
%b    = range 4 axis=global
%t    = range 4 axis=local
%k    = range 4
%ds   = mul %d 16
%br   = mul %b 4
%ao0  = add %ds %br
%ao   = add %ao0 %k
%av   = shrink %A %ao []
%a    = load %av
%bo0  = mul %k 4
%bo   = add %bo0 %t
%bv   = shrink %B %bo []
%bb   = load %bv
%cv   = shrink %acc %t []
%cur  = load %cv
%p    = mul %a %bb
%sum  = add %cur %p
%st   = store %cv %sum
%ek   = end %st %k
%et   = end %ek %t
%acc1 = after %acc %et
%u    = range 4 axis=local
%rv   = shrink %acc1 %u []
%res  = load %rv
%co0  = add %ds %br
%co   = add %co0 %u
%ov   = shrink %C %co []
%sc   = store %ov %res
%eu   = end %sc %u
%eb   = end %et %eu %b
%ed   = end %eb %d
%C1   = after %C %ed
answer.explain: Device d makes rows 4d to 4d + 3 of C, so it needs the same rows of A. Row 4d starts at element 16d, so A's offset is 16d + 4b + k, the same shard as C. The starter read 4d + 4b + k: device 1 used rows 1 to 4 of A. That offset does not follow the slice rule, so A was also replicated, and the fixed program copies 128 fewer bytes.

require: keep the device loop: %d = range 2 axis=device
